educationalCards.title: What Is a Plugged Well?
educationalCards.description: A plugged well is a well that a source agency records as permanently sealed to protect groundwater. CAPIT ensures both the original source status and the CAPIT display status remain visible.

educationalCards.title: Why Does Plugging Wells Matter?
educationalCards.description: Every properly plugged well is a permanent investment in the land, communities, and future of the United States[cite: 25]. One Well. One Token. One Permanent Record of Progress[cite: 25].

educationalCards.title: How Many Wells Remain?
educationalCards.description: Counts vary by source, definition, and publication date. CAPIT labels whether a figure refers to unplugged orphaned wells, broader inactive-well estimates, or a source-specific state inventory.
educationalCards.imageAlt: Map showing inactive wells across the United States

methodologyStrip.heading: Source-linked. Time-stamped. Revision-aware.
methodologyStrip.body: The CAPIT protocol enforces absolute cryptographic provenance for every tokenized environmental asset. By cross-referencing real-time public registries via direct flat-file and scraper pipelines, our architecture ensures immutable tracking of verification statuses, source logic, and time-stamped updates directly on the Base network.
